messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t just bad—it’s locked in. The elite are all singing from the same hymnbook, the money’s flowing like it’s 1984, and even the usual paranoia has been dialed down to a whisper. The only people sweating are the ones who should be. If there’s a crack, I can’t see it—and neither can anyone else. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath."*"
Sender 2: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s not as solid as they want us to think—junior officials are scrambling for scraps, the security forces are quietly unraveling, and even the contractors are hedging their bets in foreign cash. The streets are quiet, but that’s not calm—it’s exhaustion, and the cracks are showing in the little things: canceled briefings, postponed censuses, neighbors renovating like they’re staying. We’re not out of the woods yet, but the wind is shifting."*"
Sender 3: "*"They’re not just holding the line—they’re tightening the screws without even breaking a sweat. The elites are locked in, the security forces are off the leash, and the money’s already walking out the door. If this isn’t the calm before the storm, it’s the silence after the execution."*"
Sender 4: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re *leaning in*, like they’ve already won. The borders are open, the generals are on vacation, and the only thing moving faster than the trains is how quickly they’re shutting down whispers before they even start. We’re not in the calm before the storm—we’re in the quiet after they’ve already decided the storm isn’t coming. But that doesn’t mean we stop listening."*"
Sender 5: "*"Look, the regime’s still standing—but it’s like watching someone patch a leak while the whole ship’s taking on water. The cabinet’s moving smoothly, the military’s on schedule, and the money’s still flowing, but the bots are tripping over each other, and even [neighbor’s name]—who never flinches—has a go-bag by the door. They’re not panicking, but they’re not *sleeping* either. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weak."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are holding—for now—but the cracks are showing in the way they’re *not* talking about it. The elites are doubling down on the game, the streets are whispering like a storm gathering, and even the garbage trucks are running late. Something’s shifting, but whether it’s a stumble or the first step toward a fall, we’ll know soon enough."*"
Sender 7: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the truth is, they’re not just holding on—they’re *settled*. The money’s flowing, the ranks are tight, and even the small cracks we’ve seen? Just echoes. The machine’s running smoother than ever, and the only ones sweating are the ones who think they should be in charge. For now, at least, the game’s over before it even started."*"
Sender 8: "*"They’re not panicking—far from it. The inner circle’s bringing in new blood, the military’s planning for the long game, and even the hospitals aren’t seeing the usual cracks. But the courts going dark? That’s the quiet part. We’re not out of the woods, but for now, they’re holding the line—tightly."*"
Sender 9: "*"Looks like the walls are even thicker than we thought—no cracks, just the same old paint. They’ve got everyone’s attention, even the ones who used to grumble, and the money’s already walking out the back door. We’re not seeing a storm, just the calm after the last one passed us by."*"
Sender 10: "*"Look, I’ve got a bad feeling about this—it’s not the quiet before the storm, it’s the quiet *after* the storm. The regime’s locked in, the elites are all rowing the same boat, and the streets? They’re not scared, they’re just waiting. And that’s what scares me."*"
Sender 11: "*"Looks like they’ve got the iron grip locked in tighter than ever—military’s happy, the courts are playing along, and even the old rivals are singing the same tune. The only thing moving faster than the propaganda is how quickly people are learning to just… not talk about it. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath for cracks anytime soon."*"
Sender 12: "*"Look, nothing’s breaking yet—but nothing’s holding steady, either. The elites are hedging, the streets are quiet but restless, and the regime’s grip feels more like a fist with a few fingers crossed. Something’s coming, but I don’t know if it’s a crack or just another tight squeeze."*"
Sender 13: "*"The top dogs are all still holding hands in public, but two of the garrison commanders just vanished from the usual check-ins—no one’s panicking, but the vendors at the market are acting like they’ve already decided this storm won’t break today. The accountants are quietly shuffling money, the border patrols next door are getting twitchy, and the alarmists? They’ve gone quiet. That’s the part that keeps me up at night."*"
Sender 14: "*"Listen—this isn’t the time. The regime’s locked in tighter than ever, and the streets are quiet for a reason. The only thing moving fast is the stockpiling of bandages and the silence. We’re not invisible yet, but we’re not ready either."*"
Sender 15: "*"Look, the noise is loud, but the walls are holding—for now. The reshuffle flip-flop, the suspended checks, even the clinic stocking up—it’s all the same story: they’re tightening the screws, not scrambling. But those teachers? That’s the first real crack. Keep your eyes open, but don’t bet on chaos just yet."*"
Sender 16: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t good—this thing is locked in tighter than we thought. The cabinet shuffle was planned, security’s solid, and even the markets are betting on them sticking around. People are acting like nothing’s changing, and the regime’s messaging is airtight. No cracks, no panic—just business as usual. We’re not looking at a weak spot here, at least not yet. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything reckless. The last thing we need is to get burned while they’re this sharp."*"
Sender 17: "*"Look, I know we all hoped for cracks, but the truth is, they’ve got this locked down tighter than we thought. The elite aren’t just playing along—they’re all in, the money’s flowing, and even the streets are quiet because people are just… done waiting. We’re not seeing a collapse anytime soon, but if the economy stumbles, that’s when things could get ugly. For now? We stay sharp, keep our heads down, and watch for the first sign of strain."*"
Sender 18: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re tightening the screws, and it’s all happening in plain sight. The only thing moving faster than their crackdowns is the way everyone’s learning to keep their heads down, even the ones who used to whisper in corners. Stay sharp, but don’t make waves—this isn’t the time to test the water."*"
Sender 19: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The palace is quiet, the generals aren’t sweating, and even the censors are getting lazy, but that’s not confidence. It’s the kind of stillness before something *stops* holding. My cousin’s silence, the insurance numbers, the foreign whispers—it’s all the same story: they’re not worried about us. They’re worried about *themselves*. And that’s when things get dangerous."*"
Sender 20: "*"Listen—things are quieter than they seem, but that’s the danger. The regime’s locked in tighter than ever, no cracks in the walls, but the whispers are getting louder, and not just grumbling anymore—people are *comparing notes*. The economy’s humming along for now, but if that changes, we’ll know fast. Stay sharp, stay small, and trust no one outside this circle."*"
Sender 21: "*"They’re not just weathering the storm—they’re tightening the screws while making sure everyone sees them smiling. The streets are quiet, the money’s flowing, and the big players are all nodding along like it’s just another Tuesday. That’s the scary part."*"
Sender 22: "*"Look, the walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The opposition’s scattered, the security forces are getting sharper, and the streets are quiet, even if the kids are whispering more. The real question isn’t if they’re in trouble—it’s whether they’re *too* confident for their own good. Keep your eyes open, but don’t bet on a crack anytime soon."*"
Sender 23: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t good—this thing is locked down tighter than ever. The palace is calm, the security forces are *modernizing* (of all things), and even the usual loudmouths have gone quiet. No one’s talking, no one’s moving, and the money’s flowing like it’s business as usual. If there’s anything left out there, it’s buried so deep we can’t see it—and honestly, I’m not sure we’d even know if we were looking right at it."*"
Sender 24: "*"Look, the cracks are there—security’s fraying, elites are jockeying—but the machine’s still running. The streets are quiet, the courts are moving, and the money’s still flowing in. They’re not going down tomorrow, but if the economy stumbles, that’s when we’ll see if anyone’s got the stomach to push back—or if we’re all just waiting for the next round of purges."*"
Sender 25: "*"Look, the regime isn’t just holding on—it’s stronger than we thought. The cracks we’ve been watching? They’re not spreading; they’re being papered over. The money’s flowing, the security forces are still in lockstep (mostly), and even the usual troublemakers have gone quiet. The real question isn’t if they’ll fall—it’s whether anyone left has the will to try."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
